title: Rollback tuning using baked safety profiles and dynamic throttles
creator: Evan Brooks
description:
Goal: Define and implement automated rollback heuristics that combine precomputed safety profiles per release channel (stable, LTS, experimental) with a dynamic traffic-throttling controller. This work reduces noisy rollbacks, protects LTS audiences, and gives SREs clear tunables for progressive delivery.

Scope:
- Author safety profile schema that encodes acceptable error/rate thresholds, key metric weightings, and escalation policies per release channel.
- Build a runtime controller that adjusts ramp rate and throttles traffic when metric drift is detected, and triggers an automated rollback when multiple hard thresholds cross within a short window.
- Integrate with rollout API to support per-route overrides, ad-hoc hold, and manual abort.
- Add observability: roll-forward / rollback timeline, decision rationale, and per-cohort telemetry in Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Safety profile renderer + store (per-release) implemented and tested in staging.
- Controller can pause ramps and reduce traffic by a configurable percentage without a full rollback.
- Auto-rollback triggers when the configured combination of latency p95 increase, error-rate spikes, and end-to-end user impact score exceeds the profile thresholds for >2 consecutive evaluation windows.
- SREs/PMs can view the rollback rationale in Console and reproduce decision with a CLI simulator.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We use baked safety profiles so LTS releases have stricter thresholds; experimental channels get wider tolerance. This avoids frequent rollbacks for noisy canaries on non-LTS channels.
- Dynamic throttles (a soft-degradation step) allow temporary traffic shedding to recover without full rollback; trade-off: partial user experience degradation vs disruption from rollbacks.
- Metric selection: primary signals are request success ratio, downstream error fraction, model-quality regressions (from A/B evaluator), and latency p95. Secondary signals include CPU/GPU saturation and KV cache miss-rate.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema and storage for safety profiles (Conftable + versioning).
2) Controller prototype that subscribes to telemetry stream and computes evaluation windows (30s / 1m).
3) Throttle actuator that updates routing weights and posts events to Console.
4) Auto-rollback actuator that flips route to previous revision and records reason.
5) Hooks for manual interventions and audit logs for Private deployments.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (canary): enable profile enforcement on internal traffic only, ramp 1% -> 5% with controller in observe mode (no automated throttle/rollback) for 3 days.
- Phase B (soft control): enable throttling but not auto-rollback on trusted customers, test hold/resume flows.
- Phase C (full): enable auto-rollback for non-LTS channels, keep LTS channels in manual-rollback mode for first 2 weeks.

Risks & mitigation:
- False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks: mitigate by requiring multiple metric types and consecutive windows.
- Over-throttling causing user-visible degradation: add a minimum floor and emergency override for SRE.
- Complexity in profile management: provide sane defaults and a UI to compare profiles per release.

Next steps / tasks:
- PRD + schema draft: link in attachments.
- Implement storage + validation (ENG task).
- Prototype controller + integration tests (E2E with staging traffic generator).
- Console telemetry surfaces and rollout logs.
